### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/verify`, touching **26** documentable anchor(s).

**28** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 05a30e6ed0989d3fb604686db4f2a93093c52ad0`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 80 pages)`, `master_detail (literal, 40 pages)`
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **221** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **35** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 05a30e6ed0989d3fb604686db4f2a93093c52ad0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `411c77f6c62ddac2d6d4300af3bfe6d059c3770a` — the merge of head `0e54448624fccf2c827738caf7aca52e09459ddd` into base `05a30e6ed0989d3fb604686db4f2a93093c52ad0`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 411c77f6c62ddac2d6d4300af3bfe6d059c3770a && git checkout 411c77f6c62ddac2d6d4300af3bfe6d059c3770a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 05a30e6ed0989d3fb604686db4f2a93093c52ad0 0e54448624fccf2c827738caf7aca52e09459ddd && git checkout -B drift-repro 05a30e6ed0989d3fb604686db4f2a93093c52ad0 && git merge --no-ff 0e54448624fccf2c827738caf7aca52e09459ddd

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 05a30e6ed0989d3fb604686db4f2a93093c52ad0
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 05a30e6ed0989d3fb604686db4f2a93093c52ad0` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Contract review for card #29029 · narrowing face (`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`) · read-only reviewer at the contract-review tier, brief per `record-recognisers --brief-template --face narrowing` · 2026-11-06T00:43Z

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0e54448624fccf2c827738caf7aca52e09459ddd`
Local-runs: none
Scope: every non-prose path of the diff (34 paths: `packages/objectql/src/engine-*`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/**`, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/*.test.ts`, `packages/qa/dogfood/test/predicate-relationship-traversal.dogfood.test.ts`, `packages/verify/src/parent-write-reach*.ts`, `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/records-forms.json`) + packages/objectql/src/engine-insert.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/permission-evaluator.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/default-permission-sets.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-service.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-business-unit.object.ts, docs/adr/0090-permission-model-v2-concept-convergence.md, packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts, skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md, content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx (row 29c, read)

`reviewFace` returns no `hits` on the 39 paths, so the face is the changeset's `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`. The net diff was read three-dot against `origin/main`: 39 files, +1317 / −246, matching the PR's file list.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set of the write doors, narrowed (BREAKING) — right.** A non-system caller's `lookup` / `user` value now goes through `callerReadableReferenceExists`. That is the caller's own `find` projected to `id`, then the elevated existence probe that keeps the tenant. An id the read door does not return answers `reference_not_found`, byte-identical to a target that exists nowhere. This holds on insert (single and batch), update by id, bulk update and the `insert`-mode validate preview. `tree` stays on the elevated probe, because the rulings name `lookup` and `user` only. Multi-valued fields are judged per member. A value every landed row already stores is not re-judged (#29062, unchanged).
- **Error ordering — right.** All four doors read one predicate, `referencesCheckedBeforeRules(context) = !context.isSystem`. A non-system write checks references before `evaluateValidationRules`. A system write, including a flow run's elevated write, keeps rules first. Both orders are pinned.
- **Scope of the system-write exemption — right.** A flow run's elevated write still gets its existence check, and nothing more. Hook `ctx.api` under `runAs: 'inherit'` is judged as the caller. `sudo()` is the ruled exemption.
- **Fail closed / fail open — right, per ruling 6663849489.** A caller read that throws is refused. A target the registry does not hold is admitted, as `referenceExists` already answered.
- **`sys_user` composition with #30205 — right.** The caller's read comes first. The elevated probe with the ban fields runs only for a readable user. An unreadable user is `reference_not_found`, and its ban is never read.
- **Read widening in plugin-security — right, as ruled.** `delegatedUnitReadScope` applies only when `checkObjectPermission` refused, only to `sys_business_unit`, only to the read verbs, and only on the caller's own behalf. It admits only a non-empty `{ id: { $in: scopedUnits } }`, which is ANDed with the RLS layers and the tenant wall. No write verb is widened.
- **Public type surface.** `@objectstack/plugin-security` gains `DelegatedAdminGate#scopedBusinessUnitIds` and `delegatedUnitReadScope` (additive). The renamed `@objectstack/objectql` members are private or not re-exported. No `packages/spec` path and no authorable key moves.
- **`@objectstack/verify`.** The verifier's persona gains read on the objects its probed references name, so it moves with the rule it verifies. Right.
- **Docblocks and the #18682 persona** are retired at the producer: checklist item revision 7, the dogfood case and the docblocks. Right, per ruling 6663849489.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/29029-lookup-user-caller-read.md`: `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-security` and `@objectstack/verify` at **patch**, exactly the three packages whose product code moves. Right.
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` appear line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset. `none` is right, because what narrows is runtime data writes and no authorable key changes. A non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` with its BREAKING banner (present) and an ADR-0087 disposition (present: `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`). The upgrade sentence the ruling asked for is in the changeset. The title is `fix(objectql)!`. Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Both dev reports carry `open_questions: []` and `security_findings: none`. Ruling 6663849489 answers the four earlier open questions, and the tree implements each one as ruled.
- The declared deviations are each answered. The #30546 rig composition is pinned. The two census-gate files sit outside the named surface. The verify-persona fix and the agent-ceiling seeding fix cover the two Test Core reds, and no rule was loosened.
- **Landing constraint, not a finding:** security#1's hold (6671171164, posted on #30672) stands until security#1 posts a clear.
- Check-runs at read time: no required context failed, and several were still running. `PR-body guards` (advisory) failed only because #30672 was still open when it ran. #30672 was closed two minutes later, and the next push re-runs the check.

### ④ Design judgment

**The narrowing, read against the published spec on `main`.** The maintainer retired the existence-only lookup capability (6573561091, re-affirmed 6663849489). The #18682 persona was declared in `records-forms.json` and the engine docblocks. The PR retires it at the producer (checklist, dogfood, parity control, docblocks, doc pages) rather than narrowing it silently at a consumer. The change makes the spec's own `reference_not_found` real for a caller who cannot read the target, and leaves nothing declared that the runtime does not deliver.

**Attempts to break it**, each read in the tree at the head:
- **Doors that might skip the check:** all three engine driver writes, including the ADR-0142 precondition leg, run after it. Delete and restore write no reference.
- **The system-write exemption:** unchanged in scope.
- **Bulk update:** a value is forgiven only when every matched row stores it.
- **Ordering:** a reference the caller cannot read is answered before any rule could read it elevated.
- **The shipped member set:** `member_default` grants read on `sys_user` within the caller's own organization, so a member's `user`-field write reads its organization's users.
- **The delegate read in a full stack:** the sharing owner-match does not collapse it, the tenant wall and the `id IN` scope still AND, and switching the active organization yields no scope.
- **A new oracle:** none. Unreadable ≡ nonexistent on both the envelope and the sentence.

**Findings: none must-fix.** Six should-fix, none blocking this PR:
1. `canReadObject` / `security/explain` do not reflect the delegate's business-unit read. → follow-up card.
2. `delegatedUnitReadScope` admits `aggregate`, but the posture pins cover only `find`, `findOne` and `count`. → add an `aggregate` pin.
3. The read addition is cited in code by its ruling record only. No ADR-0090 D12 note and no adr-anchors entry exist. → next ADR-0090 touch.
4. The comment on `reference_not_found` in `packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts` still says "does not exist". → next spec touch (`packages/spec` is barred on this card).
5. The `update`-mode validate preview skips the reference check. This predates the PR. → note for the engine lane.
6. Cost: one caller `find` per reference value per row, as `master_detail` already pays. Noted.
